text:
alex: Heads up — seeing ephemeral AER + coherent reset pattern on gpu-rk17-03, started ~18:20 UTC. Batch jobs spiking latency and a few pods OOM-killed.
megan: ugh, rack17 again? any NVLink logs?
sahil: grabbing dmesg from node now, tagging @lin oncall.
ops-bot: Alert: pcie_aer_errors exceeded threshold on gpu-rk17-03 (count=12 in 10m).
alex: paste of relevant dmesg excerpt:
```
[1880123456.123456] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: AER: Multiple correctable error received: status=0x00004000
[1880123456.123789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, PID=23456, GPU=0: Xid error, channel 0x00000000
[1880123457.124000] nvlink: link down on link 1
[1880123458.124345] nvlink: link up on link 1
[1880123459.125000] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: AER: Reset request (Non-Fatal)
```
megan: that up/down every ~1s is suspicious — looks like link flapping causing AER bursts.
sahil: checking nvidia-smi error stats
```
root@gpu-rk17-03:~# nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS
GPU 0:
    Xid Errors: 9
    ECC Errors (Corrected): 14
    Volatile Uncorr. Errors: 0
```
lin: is this isolated to a single card or whole host?
alex: only GPU0 on that host so far. other nodes in rack17 show occasional AER but not same freq.
megan: could be a flaky NVLink retimer / riser / slot contact. rack17 had previous chill on slot S2. check PCI slot phys mapping.
sahil: lspci -vvv shows the device on slot 3b:00.0 with AER capabilities, running at x16 but link speed toggling between 8.0GT/s and 2.5GT/s when flaps happen.
alex: short-term mitigation: cordon + drain node to avoid job failures. plan: cordon gpu-rk17-03 and migrate running batches to spare pool.
megan: agree, also set node annotation to avoid scheduling large sequence-length workloads until we confirm hardware.
lin: I'll take on node drain. command: `kubectl cordon gpu-rk17-03 && kubectl drain gpu-rk17-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will do in 5m.
ops-bot: Action logged: node gpu-rk17-03 cordon requested by lin.
sahil: while it's draining I'll kick off memtest + vendor diagnostics: nvdiag --gpu 0 --stress 10m and vendor tool for NVLink stress.
megan: also raise RMA candidate if diagnostics fail. capture full PCI logs and timestamp to correlate with scheduler logs.
alex: can we correlate with autoscaler behavior? we saw a lot of pod restarts which may have caused transient capacity pressure in us-west-2 region.
lin: cluster autoscaler didn't trigger because reserved capacity still available, but throughput dropped ~30% for short windows. logging that for SLO/incident.
sahil: next steps: 1) drain node, 2) run nvdiag + memtest, 3) if persistent flapping -> escalate to hardware RMA for that GPU board, 4) if not, try reseat riser and test.
megan: flagging for postmortem: add NVLink link-state alert with higher granularity (1m) and add automatic lightweight throttling for long-tail latency jobs when AER > threshold.
alex: FYI I'll pin a temporary routing rule to avoid rack17 for high-SLO traffic until resolved.
lin: drain started. will post results of nvdiag in thread.
megan: thanks — one more: check kernel params `pci=noaer` as last resort if vendor wants it to stop noise while we replace hardware. Document impacts (loss of AER reporting).
ops-bot: Reminder: file an incident if customer-facing SLOs were impacted.
sahil: nvdiag started: preliminary mem test passed but NVLink stress showed 1x link drop after ~6 minutes under load.
alex: that's enough evidence for RMA. please open HW ticket with rack/shelf/slot details, include dmesg + nvdiag logs + job timestamps.
megan: I'll create the RMA ticket and block a replacement GPU. tagging hw-team. :shipit:
lin: node put into maintenance and drained. moving affected pods. last check-in in ~10m with RMA ticket id.
ops-bot: Incident candidate created: INC-2026-17433 (pending).
alex: thanks all — good quick triage. we'll follow up in postmortem for alerting rules.
